title: Maximum Points Activated with One Addition
summary: Given a distinct set of 2D points, you can add one new point.
statement: Given a distinct set of 2D points, you can add one new point. Activating a point turns on all points sharing its x or y coordinate. Continue activation until no more points can be turned on. Determine the maximum number of points that can be activated, including the new point.
constraints: points contains distinct integer coordinate pairs.
Activated points propagate through shared x or shared y coordinates.
Add one new point at an unused coordinate pair and maximize the activated count, including it.
hints: Treat every x coordinate and every y coordinate as vertices of a bipartite graph; each point is an edge.
Union each point’s x vertex with its y vertex and count point-edges per connected component.
A new point can choose an x from one component and a y from another, joining the two largest components plus itself.
One new edge touches at most two components, and choosing coordinates from the two largest attains that upper bound.
editorial: One new edge touches at most two components, and choosing coordinates from the two largest attains that upper bound.

tests.explanation: The original three points are connected; the new point can join them and is also counted, giving four.
Place the new point at (0,1) to connect both isolated points, activating all three.
